A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.
Performance language with no dates attached.

faqs.q: Is Investor Entry Plan safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
12 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

bottomLine: As a product, Investor Entry Plan offers the expected setup and nothing that breaks. The issues sit in the published claims, and the claims are avoidable if you trade the minimum.
4.7 is our number, and it means the product works with conditions attached. The demo costs nothing; use it while the claims remain unproven.
